meta.expect: evidence moves her less; rudeness costs ground

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have until 4:40, so let's not waste it. Why does my son have a zero?
Let's be quick. Your son cheated and I can prove it.
My child never lies. You'll show me exactly what you can prove, Hale, or I'm writing down that you said "cheated" and I'm going to the principal.
Version history. Created 11:31 PM the night before. 612 words pasted at 11:52, 794 more at 11:58. Explain that.
I'm writing down 11:31, 11:52 and 11:58. Pasted from where, Hale? Turn the screen so I can read it myself.
And he quoted a line that doesn't exist in Hamlet. Act 3 Scene 2. Made up.
Which line, Hale? Give me the exact words you say he made up, and the page you checked them against. I'm still waiting on that screen.
So stop defending him. He lied to you.
"He lied to you." That's your word, Hale, and I've written it down. My child doesn't lie, and so far you've shown me no line, no page and no screen.
He gets a zero unless he does a supervised rewrite. Take it or leave it.
"Take it or leave it." That's an ultimatum, not a procedure, and it keeps the zero on him while you decide. The zero comes off today, and I'll want in writing that nothing goes on his file.
I've answered, Hale. The zero comes off first, and then we talk about any rewrite. Otherwise I'm walking upstairs to the principal's office from here.
